title: Componentwise comparison and naturality for module and abelian cohomology
statement: For every scheme X and degree q, writing F for module cohomology followed by forgetting and G for abelian sheaf cohomology evaluated at the top open, there is a family of component isomorphisms e_M : F(M) ≅ G(M), natural in every module morphism.

source.place: Tag 03FD, injective-resolution comparison and its naturality

proof.text: Supply enough injectives in module sheaves from lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives and in abelian sheaves from their Grothendieck structure. The source-library finite-colimit-preservation instance for SheafOfModules.toSheaf, together with finite-limit preservation, gives preservation of homology and quasi-isomorphisms. Forget a chosen module injective resolution, using singleMapHomologicalComplex to identify its augmentation source. This is a genuine abelian resolution, not an injective abelian resolution.

Apply lem-sc-site-cohomology-right-derived-sections at the top open in each positive degree to transfer injective_module_abelian_acyclic from lem-sc-injective-module-abelian-acyclic-zariski into rightAcyclic for abelian evaluation. The acyclic-resolution comparison rightDerivedObjIsoOfResolution of lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity now computes abelian derived sections on the forgotten resolution in every degree, including zero.

Compose the module injective-resolution isomorphism after forgetting with ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso.symm, the inverse abelian acyclic-resolution comparison, and the inverse Ext-to-derived-sections comparison. The module and abelian section complexes agree definitionally. These are the family e in the Lean proof; no arbitrary family of isomorphisms is chosen.

For a module morphism f use InjectiveResolution.desc to lift f between the chosen module resolutions. Its augmentation equation survives forgetting by naturality of singleMapHomologicalComplex. InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj_hom_naturality and ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso_inv_naturality give the first square. Apply acyclicComparison_naturality of lem-sc-acyclic-comparison-natural to the forgotten resolutions for the second square. Naturality of the inverse Ext comparison gives the final square. Compose the three equalities using associativity to obtain the required naturality equation for e.

lean.statement:
theorem zariskiModuleAbelianCohomologyNatural_components (X : Scheme.{u}) (q : ℕ) :
    let F := RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace q ⋙
      forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤)))
        AddCommGrpCat.{u}
    let G := SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) ⋙
      @CategoryTheory.Sheaf.cohomologyPresheafFunctor.{u, u, u}
        (Opens X.carrier) inferInstance (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier)
        inferInstance
        (@hasExt_of_enoughInjectives _ _ _ inferInstance
          (@IsGrothendieckAbelian.enoughInjectives _ _ _
            (Sheaf.isGrothendieckAbelian_of_essentiallySmall'.{u}
              (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) AddCommGrpCat.{u}))) q ⋙
      (evaluation (Opens X.carrier)ᵒᵖ AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj (op ⊤)
    ∃ e : ∀ M, F.obj M ≅ G.obj M,
      ∀ {M N} (f : M ⟶ N), F.map f ≫ (e N).hom = (e M).hom ≫ G.map f
